title: Best ABM tools for sales and marketing teams (2026)
summary: Compare 9 ABM tools for sales and marketing teams: signal depth, contact vs account data, where outputs go, and pricing model. Updated for 2026
body_markdown:
The best ABM tools for sales and marketing teams give both sides the same target accounts, the same buyers, and the same reasons to reach out, then push that into the tools each team already uses. Account-level platforms like 6sense and Demandbase are strong for ads and intent, data tools like ZoomInfo and Clay are strong for coverage, and UserGems is the AI command center that turns contact-level buying signals into outbound and ABM actions. The right pick depends on whether your gap is data, intelligence, or execution.


## **What should sales and marketing teams look for in an ABM tool?**


Most ABM programs stall in the handoff. Marketing runs ads to an account list, sales works a different list, and nobody agrees on which buyers matter. When you evaluate tools, check five things:


- **Signal depth.** Does the tool tell you that an account is interested, or which person is interested and why? Topic intent at the account level is useful for ads. Sales needs named contacts.
- **Contact vs account level.** Account-level scoring tells you where to look. Contact-level data tells reps who to email today.
- **Where outputs go.** A dashboard nobody opens doesn't create pipeline. Look for outputs that land in your CRM, sales engagement platform (SEP), marketing automation and ad platforms.
- **Shared scoring.** One score both teams trust beats two scores that argue with each other. Ask whether the model is transparent and built on your own wins and losses.
- **Pricing model.** Platform license, credits, seats, or modular. Know what you pay for before you scale.


### Which ABM tools do sales and marketing teams use in 2026?


The most common ABM tools in 2026 are UserGems, 6sense, Demandbase, Terminus, AdRoll ABM, HubSpot, Clay, Common Room and ZoomInfo. The biggest difference between them is signal depth: most tell you which *accounts* are interested, and fewer tell you which *people* to contact and what to say.


[1. UserGems](https://www.usergems.com/)


- **Best for:** one AI command center for outbound and ABM
- **Signal depth:** your first-party data plus contact-level buying signals, such as job changes, new hires, closed-lost activity and account research
- **Contact or account level:** both, contact-first
- **Where outputs go:** your CRM, your SEP (Outreach, Salesloft, Gong Engage) and LinkedIn ads
- **Pricing model:** modular, so you can buy one agent or the full command center; quote-based, no public price list, backed by a money-back guarantee tied to pipeline


[2. 6sense](https://6sense.com/)


- **Best for:** account-level intent and predictive buying stages
- **Signal depth:** third-party topic intent, website visits and predictive models
- **Contact or account level:** account-first
- **Where outputs go:** native ads, CRM and MAP
- **Pricing model:** annual platform license with no published price. Vendr data puts the median contract around $63K a year ([source](https://www.cleanlist.ai/blog/2026-09-01-6sense-pricing-guide) )


[3. Demandbase](https://www.demandbase.com/)


- **Best for:** enterprise ABM with B2B advertising
- **Signal depth:** first- and third-party intent, account intelligence and engagement data
- **Contact or account level:** account-first
- **Where outputs go:** its own B2B-native DSP, CRM and MAP
- **Pricing model:** annual platform license, quote-based


[4. Terminus (DemandScience)](https://terminus.com/demandscience/)


- **Best for:** multichannel account ads and engagement
- **Signal depth:** engagement and intent data
- **Contact or account level:** account-first
- **Where outputs go:** native ads, email signatures and CRM
- **Pricing model:** annual license, quote-based


[5. AdRoll ABM (formerly RollWorks)](https://www.adroll.com/account-based-marketing-platform)


- **Best for:** mid-market teams starting ABM
- **Signal depth:** intent, engagement and account scoring
- **Contact or account level:** account-first
- **Where outputs go:** native ads and CRM
- **Pricing model:** packaged plans priced by demo, with ad media on CPM pricing and no minimum spend ([source](https://www.adroll.com/pricing) )


[6. HubSpot ABM tools](https://www.hubspot.com/products/abm-software)


- **Best for:** teams already running on HubSpot
- **Signal depth:** CRM activity, target account properties and ICP tiers
- **Contact or account level:** both, inside HubSpot
- **Where outputs go:** HubSpot CRM, email and ads
- **Pricing model:** included in the Professional and Enterprise tiers of Marketing Hub or Sales Hub


[7. Clay](https://www.clay.com/)


- **Best for:** custom enrichment and list building
- **Signal depth:** whatever sources you wire in, from 150+ data providers
- **Contact or account level:** both, depending on what you build
- **Where outputs go:** CRM, SEP and spreadsheets
- **Pricing model:** credit-based. Free tier, then paid plans from $167 a month billed annually ([source](https://www.clay.com/pricing) )


[8. Common Room](https://www.commonroom.io/)


- **Best for:** community, product and web signals
- **Signal depth:** person-level digital signals
- **Contact or account level:** both
- **Where outputs go:** CRM, Slack and SEP
- **Pricing model:** tiered subscription. Essential starts at $2,500 a month billed annually (5 seats, up to 100K contacts); Advanced and Enterprise are custom ([source](https://www.commonroom.io/pricing/) )


[9. ZoomInfo](https://www.zoominfo.com/)


- **Best for:** broad contact and company data
- **Signal depth:** firmographics, contacts and intent topics
- **Contact or account level:** both, database-first
- **Where outputs go:** CRM, SEP and MAP
- **Pricing model:** annual contract based on seats and credits, quote-based


#### 1. UserGems


UserGems is the AI command center for outbound and ABM. It sits between your CRM and the tools your team already uses to send emails and run ads. Data Agents capture buying signals, research accounts and find the right contacts. Intelligence Agents score accounts and contacts with a[custom scoring model](https://www.usergems.com/product/scoring) built on your own wins and losses. They also build lists, write personalized outreach and create ad audiences. Gem-E for Outbound sends emails and sequences into your SEP.[Gem-E for ABM](https://www.usergems.com/ai-agents/gem-e-for-abm) syncs audiences to LinkedIn and tracks TAM progression, so marketing and sales work the same people at the same time.


The results show up in pipeline.[Quickbase](https://www.usergems.com/customers/quickbase-2026) reports 5x leads, 3x pipeline and 2x closed-won. Docebo generated 54 enterprise opportunities in one quarter with 16% reply rates. Mimecast attributes $20M in pipeline over two years to UserGems.


**Pros**


- Contact-level signals that both sales and marketing can act on
- Transparent scoring trained on your own closed-won and closed-lost deals
- Outputs land in Salesforce, HubSpot, Outreach, Salesloft and LinkedIn, so there's no new tool for reps to adopt
- Modular: start with one agent and add more
- Money-back guarantee tied to pipeline and revenue
- 4.7 on[G2](https://www.g2.com/products/usergems/reviews) , where reviewers call out data accuracy and ease of use


**Cons**


- UserGems doesn't run ads or send email itself, so you still need a SEP and ad platforms
- Some G2 reviewers want faster signal refresh and more flexible audience filters (for example, "or" logic)


#### 2. 6sense


6sense is the best-known account-level ABM platform, built around predictive buying stages, third-party intent and native advertising. Forrester named it a Leader in[The Forrester Wave: Intent Data Providers for B2B, Q1 2025](https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20250226185842/en) , with top scores for accuracy and buying-cycle analysis.


**Pros**


- Mature account intent data and buying-stage models
- Strong for programmatic account advertising
- Wide adoption, so plenty of marketers already know it


**Cons**


- Account-level signals still leave reps guessing which person to call
- On[G2](https://www.g2.com/products/6sense-revenue-ai/reviews) , "steep learning curve" and "complex setup" are the top complaints
- No public pricing. Vendr's buyer data puts the median contract around $63K a year, with enterprise deals above $250K ([Cleanlist summary of Vendr data](https://www.cleanlist.ai/blog/2026-09-01-6sense-pricing-guide) )


More detail:[the limitations of 6sense](https://www.usergems.com/blog/limitations-of-6sense-2026) and[what 6sense really costs](https://www.usergems.com/blog/6sense-cost-pricing-transparency-and-contract-lock-in) .


#### 3. Demandbase One


Demandbase One combines account intelligence, first- and third-party intent and a B2B-native DSP for advertising. It was also named a Leader in the[Forrester Wave for B2B intent data, Q1 2025](https://www.demandbase.com/press-release/forrester-wave-leader-intent-data-q1-2025/) .


**Pros**


- Strong account-based advertising with its own DSP
- A unified account view for sales and marketing
- Built for large teams with dedicated ABM operations


**Cons**


- Account-first data, so reps still have to work out the buying group
- [G2 reviewers](https://www.g2.com/products/demandbase-one/reviews) flag a steep learning curve, heavy setup, and some false-positive intent signals
- Usually a bigger budget line than mid-market teams want


#### 4. Terminus (now part of DemandScience)


Terminus[merged into DemandScience in November 2024](https://www.demandgenreport.com/industry-news/demandscience-terminus-merge-to-create-global-revenue-marketing-company/48555/) , and the combined company runs under the DemandScience brand. Terminus focuses on multichannel account engagement: display ads, LinkedIn, email signatures and web personalization.


**Pros**


- Many engagement channels in one place
- Easy to launch account-based ad campaigns


**Cons**


- Lighter on contact-level signals for sales
- Under new ownership, ask about roadmap and product investment during evaluation


#### 5. AdRoll ABM (formerly RollWorks)


RollWorks was[folded into the AdRoll brand in August 2025](https://markets.financialcontent.com/stocks/article/gnwcq-2025-8-27-adroll-unifies-under-one-brand-empowering-marketers-with-an-ai-powered-connected-advertising-platform) and is now sold as[AdRoll ABM](https://help.adroll.com/hc/en-us/articles/38252885086093-What-is-AdRoll-ABM) . It's a practical entry point for mid-market teams that want account targeting, scoring and ads.


**Pros**


- Approachable setup with tiered plans
- Well-regarded HubSpot integration and customer support (4.3 on[G2](https://www.g2.com/products/rollworks/reviews) )


**Cons**


- Account-level focus, so reviewers mention limited contact-level visibility
- Reporting and attribution are less flexible than enterprise platforms


#### 6. HubSpot ABM tools


HubSpot includes target accounts, buying roles, ICP tiers and a target accounts dashboard inside the CRM, available on Professional and Enterprise tiers of Marketing Hub or Sales Hub.


**Pros**


- No new tool to adopt if you already run on HubSpot
- Marketing and sales share one record


**Cons**


- Signals mostly reflect activity inside HubSpot. External buying signals and contact discovery need another layer.
- [G2 reviewers](https://www.g2.com/products/hubspot-marketing-hub/reviews) note gaps for advanced ABM, such as landing pages that can't personalize by target account and awkward account-level deal attribution


#### 7. Clay


Clay is a flexible enrichment and workflow builder. It chains[150+ data providers](https://www.clay.com/pricing) with AI research steps in a spreadsheet-style interface. Paid plans start at $167 a month, billed annually, and run on credits.


**Pros**


- Very customizable; strong for technical RevOps and growth teams
- Waterfall enrichment improves coverage
- 4.6 on[G2](https://www.g2.com/products/clay-com-clay/reviews)


**Cons**


- You build and maintain the logic yourself; G2's top complaint is the learning curve
- Credit use can be hard to predict at scale
- Marketing and sales still need a shared scoring layer on top


How it compares head to head:[UserGems vs Clay](https://www.usergems.com/usergems-vs-clay) .


#### 8. Common Room


[Common Room](https://www.commonroom.io/) unifies signals from CRM, product usage, web, community and social activity. It resolves them to people with its Person360 identity layer and runs RoomieAI agents on top.


**Pros**


- Strong person-level digital signals
- A great fit for product-led and community-heavy companies
- 4.5 on[G2](https://www.g2.com/products/common-room/reviews) , with high marks for support


**Cons**


- Value depends on how much digital and community activity your buyers produce
- G2 reviewers call the HubSpot integration "somewhat hacky" and question deanonymization accuracy
- Ad audience workflows are lighter than dedicated ABM platforms


#### 9. ZoomInfo


ZoomInfo now calls itself a go-to-market intelligence platform and[trades under the ticker GTM](https://pipeline.zoominfo.com/sales/zoominfo-ticker-change-from-zi-to-gtm) . It pairs its large B2B contact and company database with intent topics, Copilot and GTM Studio workflows.


**Pros**


- Broad contact and company coverage
- Familiar to most sales teams; 4.5 on[G2](https://www.g2.com/products/zoominfo-salesos/reviews) across 9,000+ reviews


**Cons**


- Data alone doesn't tell you who to prioritize or why
- G2 reviewers often cite stale job titles and high pricing
- Contract structure can be complex


## **How do you choose the right ABM tool for both teams?**


Start with the gap you feel most:


- **"We don't know who to target."** You need contact-level signals and a scoring model both teams trust. Look at UserGems or Common Room. Our guide to[contact-based marketing tools](https://www.usergems.com/blog/contact-based-marketing-tools) goes deeper.
- **"We need account ads at scale."** Demandbase, 6sense, Terminus or AdRoll ABM run ads natively.
- **"Our data is thin."** ZoomInfo or Clay add coverage. Plan for who owns the logic.
- **"Sales and marketing work different lists."** You need a shared layer that sends the same audience to the SEP and to[LinkedIn Matched Audiences](https://business.linkedin.com/marketing-solutions/ad-targeting/matched-audiences) . That is the job of a command center. Here is[how coordinated sales and marketing ABM works](https://www.usergems.com/aeo-content-hub/coordinated-sales-and-marketing-abm-how-to-target-the-same-people-at-the-same-time) in practice.


Many teams pair one execution platform with one intelligence layer. For example, keep your SEP and LinkedIn Campaign Manager, and add[Gem-E for ABM](https://www.usergems.com/ai-agents/gem-e-for-abm) to decide who goes into each audience and when.


## **FAQ**


### **What is the difference between an ABM platform and an ABM tool?**


An ABM platform usually bundles data, scoring and ads in one contract. An ABM tool solves one part, like enrichment, ads or scoring. Most B2B teams end up with a mix.


### **Do ABM tools work for outbound sales?**


Some do. Account-level tools help marketing more than reps. Tools with contact-level signals and SEP integrations, like UserGems, help reps decide who to contact and what to say.


### **Which ABM tool is best for mid-market B2B companies?**


Mid-market teams often start with HubSpot ABM tools or AdRoll ABM for ads, then add a signal and scoring layer such as UserGems when they need named buyers for outbound.


### **How do sales and marketing share ABM data?**


Use one account and contact score, one target list, and push it to both the SEP and ad platforms from the same source. That avoids two teams chasing two lists.


### **Is 6sense required to run ABM?**


No. Many teams run ABM with their CRM, a SEP, LinkedIn ads and a contact-level signal layer. The right stack depends on budget and team size.
